name: chem-r6
context:
Round 6. You returned REVISE last round on reaction scoring for a chemistry puzzle game. It is now BUILT and MEASURED. Review the measurements.

YOUR FINDING (c) AND THE VERDICT: you called conservation of mass a 'Brittle Constraint' — that a player could select a connected region of molecules that 'simply cannot be mathematically partitioned into the 16 library molecules', making the game feel like a broken math puzzle — and said the constraint must be relaxed or the library expanded.

WE MEASURED IT AND DID NOT DO WHAT YOU ASKED. Over 1800 random selections, a valid partition exists 100.0% of the time at every selection size. This is necessary rather than lucky: the reactants are themselves library molecules, so the arrangement the player started with is always a valid product set. Conservation of mass cannot be unsatisfiable. Relaxing it would have discarded a physical law to fix a problem that does not exist.

Your instinct was right under a different mechanism. At 2 reactants only 17.2% of selections have an EXOTHERMIC rearrangement; at 3 it is 39.3%, at 4 it is 55.8%. So most small selections do nothing. That is a dud move rather than a broken puzzle. Our fix is to the INFORMATION rather than the constraint: the game enumerates every selection that actually reacts and the player chooses among live options, never guessing. The same pattern already guarantees no dead boards.

YOUR FINDING (a): you predicted reaction scoring would decouple the linear correlation but that a 'mass proxy' would persist. Measured, using the identical instrument that falsified the previous design:

                              assembly scoring    reaction scoring
    correlation(size, score)      0.843               0.122
    concept minus instinct      +1.43%  t=1.23      +35.5%  t=15.07
    instinct minus random       +8.37%  t=4.13      -21.0%  t=-11.73

'Instinct' is a policy that takes the largest selection — the match-3 heuristic, requiring no chemistry. 'Concept' is a policy that prefers reactions whose REACTANTS are weakly bonded, i.e. a player who understood that a strongly-bonded molecule has little left to give, and who memorised no numbers at all. Full knowledge of the bond-energy table is worth +73.7% at t=23.71.

Under assembly scoring the match-3 instinct was the most valuable thing a player could bring. Under reaction scoring it is actively harmful: the largest selection loses to a random one on 129 of 150 boards.

CHEMISTRY THE ENGINE DERIVES, none of it special-cased: CH4 + 2 O2 gives CO2 + 2 H2O at +808 kJ/mol (textbook 802-818); 3 H2 + N2 gives 2 NH3 at +97 (Haber process, real value about -92 so +92 released); 2 H2O2 gives 2 H2O + O2 at +203 (real about 196); and N2 + O2 is REFUSED because making nitric oxide from air is endothermic.

An oracle asserts the decoupling, the concept's positive uplift, the instinct's NEGATIVE uplift, and all four of those reactions.

questions.text: Do you accept that conservation of mass is not brittle, given that the identity partition always exists, or is there a case we have missed?
Is enumerating every reactive selection for the player the right fix for the 83% dud rate at two reactants, or does showing the player all live moves destroy the puzzle?
The match-3 instinct now scores WORSE than random. Is that a good property or a usability trap for players arriving from other match-3 games?
Is a +35.5% uplift at t=15.07 for a memorisation-free chemical concept sufficient to justify claiming this game teaches chemistry?
Name the most specific real chemistry this built design still teaches wrongly.
